panels.title: House used
panels.description: Energy the house consumed over the selected range. House load is not metered: it is solar production plus grid power, per quarter-hour. A quarter-hour only counts once the grid meter and (in daylight) the main array have both reported, so the newest quarter-hour is usually blank.

targets.rawQueryText:
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT (CAST(strftime('%s', s.ts) AS INTEGER) / 900) * 900 AS t,
         so.slug AS slug,
         SUM(s.value * s.duration_s) / SUM(s.duration_s) AS w
  FROM core_sample s
  JOIN core_series se ON se.id = s.series_id
  JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
  WHERE se.metric IN ('production_w', 'demand_w')
    AND s.ts >= datetime(($__from / 1000 / 900) * 900, 'unixepoch')
    AND s.ts <  datetime($__to / 1000, 'unixepoch')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
), gb AS (
  -- PG&E's own hourly meter history (Green Button import), spread evenly
  -- over the hour's quarters. Used only where the Eagle has no reading.
  SELECT (CAST(strftime('%s', s.ts) AS INTEGER) / 900) * 900 + o.off AS t,
         'pge' AS slug,
         SUM(CASE WHEN se.metric = 'grid_import_wh' THEN s.value ELSE -s.value END)
           * 3600.0 / MAX(s.duration_s) AS w
  FROM core_sample s
  JOIN core_series se ON se.id = s.series_id
  JOIN (SELECT 0 AS off UNION ALL SELECT 900 UNION ALL SELECT 1800 UNION ALL SELECT 2700) o
    ON o.off < s.duration_s
  WHERE se.metric IN ('grid_import_wh', 'grid_export_wh')
    AND s.ts >= datetime(($__from / 1000 / 3600) * 3600 - 3600, 'unixepoch')
    AND s.ts <  datetime($__to / 1000, 'unixepoch')
  GROUP BY s.ts, o.off
  HAVING COUNT(*) = 2
), p AS (
  SELECT t,
         MAX(CASE WHEN slug = 'solaredge' THEN w END) AS main,
         MAX(CASE WHEN slug = 'envoy' THEN w END) AS guest,
         COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN slug = 'eagle' THEN w END),
                  MAX(CASE WHEN slug = 'pge' THEN w END)) AS grid,
         MAX(slug = 'eagle') AS live_grid
  FROM (SELECT t, slug, w FROM raw
        UNION ALL
        SELECT t, slug, w FROM gb
        WHERE t >= ($__from / 1000 / 900) * 900 AND t < $__to / 1000)
  GROUP BY t
), b AS (
  SELECT t, main, guest, grid,
         COALESCE(main, 0) + COALESCE(guest, 0) AS solar,
         CASE WHEN grid IS NOT NULL
               AND (main IS NOT NULL OR COALESCE(guest, 0) < 20)
               AND sl + grid >= 0
              THEN sl + grid END AS load
  FROM (SELECT p.*,
               -- An hourly PG&E reading pairs with the hour's mean solar;
               -- per-quarter solar against an hourly grid figure would go
               -- negative whenever production swung within the hour.
               CASE WHEN live_grid = 1
                    THEN COALESCE(main, 0) + COALESCE(guest, 0)
                    ELSE AVG(COALESCE(main, 0) + COALESCE(guest, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY t / 3600)
               END AS sl
        FROM p)
)
SELECT SUM(load) * 900 / 3600.0 / 1000.0 AS v FROM b WHERE load IS NOT NULL

panels.title: Peak draw vs. 200 A
panels.description: Highest current pulled from PG&E over the selected range, against the 200 A main. The amber mark is 160 A, the 80% a breaker is rated to carry continuously. Amps are the Eagle's whole-house watts over a nominal 240 V, so they assume the two legs are evenly loaded; a heavy 120 V load puts more than this on one leg. Only the Eagle (from Aug 2026) reads fast enough for this — PG&E's hourly history would hide every peak, so earlier ranges show nothing.

panels.title: Current through the service — 200 A at the top
panels.description: Current at the meter: up toward the 200 A main while the house draws from PG&E, below zero while the arrays push power back. Each point is the peak (or deepest dip) within it. The dashed lines are the 200 A main and 160 A continuous rating. Amps are the Eagle's whole-house watts over a nominal 240 V, so they assume the two legs are evenly loaded; a heavy 120 V load puts more than this on one leg. Only the Eagle (from Aug 2026) reads fast enough for this — PG&E's hourly history would hide every peak, so earlier ranges show nothing.

targets.rawQueryText:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT (CAST(strftime('%s', s.ts) AS INTEGER) / MAX(10, $__interval_ms / 1000)) * MAX(10, $__interval_ms / 1000) AS t,
         MAX(MAX(s.value, 0)) / 240.0 AS draw,
         MIN(MIN(s.value, 0)) / 240.0 AS back
  FROM core_sample s
  JOIN core_series se ON se.id = s.series_id
  JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
  WHERE so.slug = 'eagle' AND se.metric = 'demand_w'
    AND s.ts >= datetime($__from / 1000, 'unixepoch')
    AND s.ts <  datetime($__to / 1000, 'unixepoch')
  GROUP BY 1
), ticks(t) AS (
  SELECT ($__from / 1000 / MAX(10, $__interval_ms / 1000)) * MAX(10, $__interval_ms / 1000)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT t + MAX(10, $__interval_ms / 1000) FROM ticks WHERE t + MAX(10, $__interval_ms / 1000) < $__to / 1000
)
-- The peak and the deepest dip in each bucket, so neither averages away.
SELECT ticks.t AS time,
       a.draw AS "Drawing from PG&E",
       a.back AS "Sending back"
FROM ticks
LEFT JOIN a ON a.t = ticks.t
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: ${loads}
panels.description: Power drawn by one load with its own meter. Each metered load gets its own chart, since a computer's watts and a car charger's kilowatts can't share an axis; pick which ones with Loads at the top. Appliances join as their collectors are added, with no dashboard edit. Each point is the average over its stretch of time; a gap means that load wasn't read, not that it was off.

targets.rawQueryText:
WITH loads AS (
  -- Every metered load: any power series that isn't a source of energy
  -- or the grid meter. New appliance collectors appear here on their own.
  SELECT se.id AS series_id, so.name AS name
  FROM core_series se
  JOIN core_source so ON so.id = se.source_id
  WHERE so.kind NOT IN ('solar', 'grid', 'gas') AND se.unit = 'W'
    AND so.name IN (${loads:sqlstring})
), k AS (
  SELECT MAX(300, $__interval_ms / 1000) AS step
), ticks(t) AS (
  SELECT ($__from / 1000 / (SELECT step FROM k)) * (SELECT step FROM k)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT t + (SELECT step FROM k) FROM ticks WHERE t + (SELECT step FROM k) < $__to / 1000
), x AS (
  SELECT s.series_id, CAST(strftime('%s', s.ts) AS INTEGER) AS st,
         CAST(strftime('%s', s.ts) AS INTEGER) + s.duration_s AS en, s.value
  FROM core_sample s
  JOIN loads l ON l.series_id = s.series_id
  WHERE s.ts >= datetime($__from / 1000 - 86400, 'unixepoch')
    AND s.ts <  datetime($__to / 1000, 'unixepoch')
)
-- Each point is the mean over the part of its bucket the samples cover
-- (a 30-minute reading spans several 5-minute buckets); no sample at all
-- leaves a gap.
SELECT ticks.t AS time, l.name AS load,
       SUM(x.value * (MIN(x.en, ticks.t + k.step) - MAX(x.st, ticks.t)))
         / SUM(MIN(x.en, ticks.t + k.step) - MAX(x.st, ticks.t)) AS value
FROM ticks
CROSS JOIN k
CROSS JOIN loads l
LEFT JOIN x ON x.series_id = l.series_id AND x.st < ticks.t + k.step AND x.en > ticks.t
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2
